title: Redis Patterns: Cache, Session & Leaderboard
concept: Use Redis where it earns its place and keep PostgreSQL as the source of truth: cache-aside with deliberate TTLs and invalidation, sessions with sliding expiry, rate limiting, sorted-set leaderboards with top N and rank, rebuilds from the database, versioned updates, and handling duplicate and out-of-order events. Exercises run on an in-memory Redis with a fake clock.
description: An advanced course for backend developers adding Redis to a real application. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - a course page that shows the old title for an hour, sessions that never expire, a submission endpoint hammered by one user, a leaderboard that lost its scores when Redis restarted, a late event that overwrote a newer score - and fixes it with the right structure and a test that proves it: strings, hashes and sorted sets chosen by access pattern, cache-aside and invalidation, TTL and sliding expiry, fixed-window rate limits, top N and rank, writing the database first, idempotent rebuilds, version checks, and the production side of eviction, persistence and stampedes. 11 lessons with evidence-based quizzes and TypeScript challenges on a deterministic in-memory Redis.
